content: We cannot change the past, but we can change our attitude toward it and liberate its creative energy.
author: Carl Jung
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. True art and creative work are not about clever technique; they demand total emotional skin in the game. When you create safely to please an audience or avoid criticism, the work feels hollow and bloodless.

In Carl Jung's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Pouring your genuine spirit, vulnerability, and raw lived experience into what you make is what gives it enduring life. The work that resonates across centuries is always the work created with unapologetic personal truth.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
